title: Are we heading for World War Three? | The Global Story
summary: Historian Margaret MacMillan on whether the 2026 US-Israel war with Iran could become a world war: accidents and pride drive escalation, but Russia and China are unlikely to join.

assertions.quote: it's not foolish or imagining things to be worried about conflict spreading at the moment.
I doubt if they'll be drawn in militarily. Why would they want to be?
it's quite possible that China may decide to make a move against Taiwan because again other powers are distracted.

verdicts.note: Opportunism is a known pattern, but whether Beijing or Moscow would act on it is a matter of intent.
CSIS warns that during a US-China war Russia, North Korea or Iran 'might take advantage of U.S. distraction', the same opportunism mechanism but in the reverse direction from the claim.

assertions.quote: a lot of what set it off finally was accident, and people misjudging their opponents, and people feeling they didn't dare back down.

verdicts.note: Historians debate it: miscalculation mattered in 1914, but most major wars also involved deliberate decisions.

CSIS notes 'wars happen' because nations miscalculate the balance, get swept along in a crisis or act on domestic politics; miscalculation is one cause among several, not shown to dominate over deliberate plans.

Braumoeller: the largest wars come from a series of reasonable-seeming decisions by leaders who will not accept defeat, escalating without anyone intending a catastrophe; this is unintended escalation rather than pure accident.

assertions.quote: I think the whole thing about how how it's easier to start a war than it is to end it.
how close we came to an all-out nuclear war because the Soviets had persuaded themselves they were about to be attacked
the reason for that was largely I think because of nuclear weapons
Britain and Germany were each other's biggest trading partners before the First World War.
But I don't think that is the same as World War III.
he can't back down, but he's not winning.

verdicts.note: DDIS: Russia is gaining ground and better placed for attrition, but has taken only about 1% of Ukraine's territory by 2025, remains far from victory, and neither side is likely to make significant advances in 2026.
US intelligence (March 2026) says Russia has kept the upper hand over the past year and is confident it will prevail on the battlefield.
Eurasia Group (January 2026) says Ukraine's position is deteriorating but expects no immediate breakthrough for either side.
The Munich Security Report (February 2026) says Russia is 'seemingly regaining tactical initiative along parts of the front'.
